unit.title: Present-Tense -ar Verbs: One Pattern, Hundreds of Verbs

lesson.title: Six Sentences: What My Family Does Every Day
lesson.subject: spanish

contentBlocks.text: You have drilled the pattern and used it out loud. Today you put it on paper: six sentences about what the people in your family do every day. This is the first time this year you write several original sentences in a row that are all your own — not a frame with one blank, but full sentences you build from the pattern.

Almost every sentence today is about someone other than you, so you mostly need two forms:

- One family member -> the él/ella form (-a): Mi mamá trabaja en una tienda. Mi hermano estudia mucho.
- Two or more -> the ellos form (-an): Mis hermanos miran mucha televisión. Mis abuelos hablan español.

And for one sentence about you together with them, use nosotros (-amos): Mi familia y yo hablamos español en casa. Watch the collective words: mi familia is one word for the whole group, so it takes the él/ella form — Toda mi familia necesita un descanso.

Family words you already know, to be the subjects of your sentences:

mi madre / mi mamá, mi padre / mi papá, mi hermano, mi hermana, mis hermanos, mis padres, mi abuelo, mi abuela, mis abuelos, mi tío, mi tía.

You can also use a name: Mi primo Daniel usa la computadora toda la tarde.

Here is a finished set of six. Read how each verb matches its subject:

1. Mi papá trabaja en un restaurante.
2. Mi mamá enseña inglés en una escuela.
3. Mi hermana estudia en la universidad.
4. Mis abuelos hablan español y un poco de inglés.
5. Mi hermano y yo miramos fútbol los domingos.
6. Toda mi familia necesita un día de descanso.

Sentence 4 has two people -> hablan. Sentence 5 is 'my brother and I' -> miramos. Sentence 6 has the collective mi familia -> necesita.

Make a few sentences longer with connectors you already use:

- y — and: Mi hermana estudia mucho y trabaja los sábados.
- también — also: Mi tío enseña matemáticas. Mi tía también enseña.
- pero — but: Mis padres hablan español, pero mi hermano habla más inglés.
- por eso — so, that's why: Mi mamá trabaja mucho, por eso necesita un descanso.

When a second verb has the same subject, you do not repeat the subject: Mi hermana estudia y trabaja.

Six sentences, each with a -ar verb that agrees with its subject — that is real writing in Spanish. Tomorrow you interview a partner out loud and report what they told you to the class, then take the week's quiz.

items.sentence: Mis primos ___ mucha televisión los fines de semana.
Mi familia y yo ___ español en casa.
Mi hermano ___ una computadora para hacer la tarea.
Mis padres ___ más tiempo para descansar.

objectives: Write six original sentences about family members' daily activities, each with a regular -ar verb that agrees with its subject
Choose the él/ella form for one person, the ellos form for two or more, and the nosotros form for 'my family and I,' including with collective subjects like mi familia (él/ella form)
Join sentences with y, también, pero, and por eso, dropping the repeated subject when a second verb shares it
materialsNeeded: Device for the cloze activity (optional — can be done orally)
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Warm-up: sort ten subjects aloud into 'one person' (él/ella, -a) and 'more than one' (ellos, -an): mi tía, mis tíos, mi abuelo, mis padres, mi hermana...
2. Teach the collective-subject point: mi familia and toda mi familia are singular -> necesita, trabaja.
3. Review the family words. Students may use names.
4. Read the model six sentences together; for each, name the subject and why the ending fits.
5. Teach the four connectors and the drop-the-repeated-subject rule (estudia y trabaja).
6. Students draft their six sentences. Circulate and check subject-verb agreement, not content.
7. Play the cloze activity, then complete the worksheet.
8. Preview tomorrow: partner interviews, report-outs, and the quiz.
differentiationTips: Struggling: provide six sentence stems (Mi ___ ___ ...) with the subject given and a word bank of the eight verbs; the student supplies the ending and finishes the thought
Ready for more: require eight sentences, at least two with a connector, and at least one nosotros sentence, then have them translate three into English
If a child writes 'Mis padres trabaja,' point to the subject: 'How many? More than one -> the ending is -an: trabajan.'
teacherGuide.answerKey: Sentences vary. A correct sentence has a -ar verb whose ending matches its subject: one person -> -a (Mi mamá trabaja...), two or more -> -an (Mis abuelos hablan...), 'my family and I' -> -amos (Mi familia y yo hablamos...), a collective subject like mi familia -> -a (Toda mi familia necesita...). Connectors: y, también, pero, por eso; a shared second verb drops the repeated subject (Mi hermana estudia y trabaja). Model set: 1. Mi papá trabaja en un restaurante. 2. Mi mamá enseña inglés en una escuela. 3. Mi hermana estudia en la universidad. 4. Mis abuelos hablan español y un poco de inglés. 5. Mi hermano y yo miramos fútbol los domingos. 6. Toda mi familia necesita un día de descanso. Cloze: 1. trabaja, 2. miran, 3. hablamos, 4. usa, 5. necesitan.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Fulfills the scope-and-sequence Day 4 design — 'write 6 sentences about what your family members do daily' — as the presentational-writing checkpoint inside the week's WA-WL-2015.1.1 arc. It is the year's first sustained original production: weeks 1-6 asked for single frames or short exchanges, and this task requires six independent sentences whose verbs each agree with a chosen subject. The él/ella vs. ellos choice and the collective-noun case (mi familia -> necesita) are the exact agreement decisions Friday's quiz assesses, and the connector work feeds the paragraph-length output the -er/-ir week and the preterite weeks build toward.

generationData.instructions: One person -> -a. Two or more -> -an. My family and I -> -amos. A collective word like mi familia counts as one -> -a.

rows.problem: Write the correct form: 'Mi madre ___ (trabajar) en una oficina.'   'Mis padres ___ (llegar) a casa a las seis.'   'Mi familia y yo ___ (mirar) películas los viernes.'
One family member or more than one? Choose the ending: 'Mi hermana ___ (estudiar) por la noche.' and 'Mis hermanas ___ (estudiar) por la noche.'
Write 6 sentences about what your family members do every day. Use at least four different -ar verbs from this week.
Circle every verb in your 6 sentences. Next to each, write the pronoun it matches (él/ella, ellos, or nosotros).
